en: to be sound; to be healthy

examples.en: If you have a wholesome hobby, your stress decreases.
This game is wholesome even for children.
The habit of spending money sensibly is important.
Don't visit sites that aren't wholesome.
They say that if your body is healthy, your mind becomes sound too.

examples.ko: 회사 재정이 건전해서 오래 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: The company's finances are sound, so I want to work there a long time.

explain: '건강하다'는 몸이나 마음의 상태가 좋을 때 쓰고, '건전하다'는 생각, 취미, 문화, 재정이 바르고 문제가 없을 때 써요. '건전한 생각', '건전 가요'처럼 쓰고, 몸이 튼튼하다는 말은 보통 '건강하다'를 써요. 반대말은 '불건전하다'예요.

phrases.en: There are many people with sound thinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이 바르고 문제가 없다는 칭찬의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment meaning the thinking is proper and without problems.

phrases.en: This movie isn't wholesome for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내용이나 분위기가 바람직하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when content or atmosphere is not wholesome.

phrases.nuance_ko: 돈 쓰는 방식이 바르고 무리가 없다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for spending that is sensible and not excessive.

explain_en: 건강하다 is for a good state of body or mind, while 건전하다 is for thoughts, hobbies, culture, or finances that are proper and free of problems. It appears in 건전한 생각 (a sound way of thinking) and 건전 가요 (clean pop songs); for a strong body, people usually say 건강하다. The opposite is 불건전하다.

examples.en: Many people hope for Korean reunification.

examples.ko: 남북통일이 되면 기차로 유럽까지 갈 수 있을까요?
examples.en: If the Koreas were reunified, could we travel to Europe by train?
We learned about Korean reunification in class today.
Our class debated the topic of Korean reunification.

examples.ko: 할머니는 남북통일을 꼭 보고 싶다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother said she really wants to see reunification.
We talked about how much reunification would cost.

explain: 뉴스나 수업에서는 '통일'이라고만 줄여 말할 때도 많아요. '통일을 하다'보다는 '통일이 되다', '통일을 이루다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '평화통일'도 자주 나와요.

phrases.nuance_en: A common short form of 남북통일.

phrases.en: If reunification happens, where do you want to go?
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 되다 to mean that reunification takes place.

phrases.en: Many people hope for peaceful reunification.

explain_en: In the news and in class it is often shortened to just '통일'. People usually say '통일이 되다' or '통일을 이루다' rather than '통일을 하다'. A related term you will often see is '평화통일'.

examples.en: The risk of earthquakes is ever-present everywhere.
The possibility of accidents is always there, so be careful.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에는 갈등이 상존하고 있어요.
examples.en: Conflict constantly exists between the two countries.
Even though the danger was always there, nobody knew.

examples.ko: 문제가 상존하는 한 불안은 사라지지 않아요.
examples.en: As long as the problem persists, the anxiety won't go away.
Even a small risk should be prepared for if it's always present.

explain: 위험, 문제, 갈등처럼 좋지 않은 것이 늘 있을 때 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '늘 있다'라고 하고, '상존하다'는 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: There are constant dangers at sea, so please be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상존하다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 형태로, 늘 있는 위험이나 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used for dangers or problems that are always present.

phrases.example: 두 나라 사이에 갈등이 아직도 상존하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Conflict still remains between the two countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 계속 남아 있다는 뜻으로 뉴스나 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it still continues to exist; common in news and writing.

phrases.example: 집 안에도 작은 사고의 위험이 늘 있어요.
phrases.en: There is always a risk of small accidents even at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상존하다'의 쉬운 말로, 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say '상존하다' in conversation.

explain_en: It is mostly used for unwelcome things like risks, problems, or conflicts that are always present. In daily talk people say '늘 있다', while '상존하다' appears more in news and writing.

examples.en: Korea and Vietnam established diplomatic relations in 1992.

examples.ko: 수교 삼십 주년을 기념하는 행사가 열렸어요.
examples.en: An event marking the thirtieth anniversary of diplomatic ties was held.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 수교 이후 교류가 크게 늘었어요.
examples.en: Since establishing relations, exchanges between the two countries have grown a lot.
The number of countries with diplomatic ties grew gradually.
We learned about the process of establishing relations in history class.
Thanks to diplomatic relations, flight routes were also created.

explain: 수교는 나라와 나라가 정식으로 외교 관계를 맺는 거예요. 보통 '수교하다', '수교를 맺다'로 쓰고, 한국과 다른 나라의 사이를 말할 때 '수교 몇 주년'이라고 해요. 관계를 끊는 건 '단교'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The two countries established diplomatic relations long ago.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수교하다, saying the relationship is 'formed'.

phrases.example: 수교 이후 두 나라 사이의 여행이 늘었어요.
phrases.en: Since the establishment of relations, travel between the two countries has increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수교한 때부터 지금까지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the period from when relations began until now.

phrases.en: The two countries formally establish relations this year.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding -하다 to the noun 수교.

explain_en: 수교 is two countries formally starting diplomatic relations. It is usually used as 수교하다 or 수교를 맺다, and anniversaries are called 수교 몇 주년. Cutting those ties is called 단교.

en: to be composed; to be refined

examples.ko: 친구에게 빌린 돈도 엄연한 빚이니까 약속한 날에 갚아야 해요.
examples.en: Money borrowed from a friend is still a real debt, so you must repay it on the promised day.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 작아도 엄연히 정식 회사예요.
examples.en: This shop is small, but it is undeniably a proper company.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 실력에는 엄연한 차이가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a clear difference in skill between the two of them.

examples.ko: 엄연히 규칙이 있는데도 지키지 않는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Even though there is clearly a rule, many people don't follow it.
No matter how much you deny it, that is a plain fact.

examples.ko: 저는 엄연히 성인인데 아직도 아이 취급을 받아요.
examples.en: I am very much an adult, yet I'm still treated like a child.

explain: 부정하기 어려울 만큼 분명하게 있다는 느낌이에요. 주로 '엄연한 사실/현실/차이', '엄연히'의 모양으로 쓰고, 말할 때는 '엄연히 ~인데요'처럼 상대 말에 반박할 때 잘 나와요.

phrases.example: 그가 거짓말을 한 것은 엄연한 사실이에요.
phrases.en: It is an undeniable fact that he lied.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정할 수 없이 분명한 일을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for something clear and undeniable.

phrases.en: This is clearly my seat, you know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대 말에 반박할 때 '엄연히 ~인데요'처럼 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to push back, as in '엄연히 ~인데요'.

phrases.example: 비슷해 보여도 두 말에는 엄연한 차이가 있어요.
phrases.en: Even though they look alike, there is a clear difference between the two words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷해 보이는 것 사이에 분명한 차이가 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say there is a real difference between things that seem alike.

explain_en: It carries the feeling that something clearly exists and is hard to deny. It appears mostly as '엄연한 사실/현실/차이' or '엄연히', and in speech it often shows up when pushing back, as in '엄연히 ~인데요'.

en: to oust; to expel; to drive out

examples.en: The assembly ousted its leader from his position.
Citizens demanded that the corrupt politician be driven out.
The shareholders held a meeting to oust the president.

examples.ko: 그 단체는 규칙을 어긴 회원을 축출하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The group decided to expel the member who broke the rules.

examples.ko: 침입한 세력을 나라에서 축출하는 데 성공했어요.
examples.en: They succeeded in driving the invading force out of the country.

examples.ko: 반대파를 축출한 뒤 그는 혼자 권력을 잡았어요.
examples.en: After ousting the opposition, he took power alone.

explain: '쫓아내다'나 '내쫓다'를 더 딱딱하게 한 말이에요. 뉴스나 역사에서 권력자, 정치 세력, 조직의 구성원을 내보낼 때 주로 써요. '권좌에서 축출하다'처럼 자리나 장소를 같이 말해요.

phrases.en: The owner kicked the noisy customer out of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '축출하다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요. 일상에서 널리 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language version of 축출하다, widely used in daily life.
phrases.en_equiv: to drive out; to kick out

phrases.en: That politician was eventually expelled from the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: '축출하다'의 피동 표현으로, 쫓겨나는 쪽을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the person being expelled is the subject.

phrases.en: The crowd ousted the dictator from power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 권력의 자리에서 사람을 내보낸다는 뜻으로 뉴스나 역사에서 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means removing someone from a seat of power; appears in news and history.

explain_en: It is a stiffer version of '쫓아내다' or '내쫓다'. It is mostly used in news and history for removing a ruler, political force or organization member. It is often paired with a position or place, as in '권좌에서 축출하다'.
